messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: R optimization level?
parts:
It's taking forever for models to compile for me in
the new RStan 2.5. Seems like at least twice as long
as it used to, but I may be imagining things.

I want to make sure that in my RStan that I'm using
clang++ and -O3. How do I do that?

Also, see my post to stan-dev about setting mtune. Right now,
it's set to core2, which isn't my architecture.

With Rob's help, I tracked down ~/.R/Makevars:

|
CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++
CXXFLAGS = -mtune=core2 -O3 $(LTO) #set_by_rstan
R_XTRA_CPPFLAGS = -I$(R_INCLUDE_DIR) #set_by_rstanCC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256
CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256
CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256

CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256

CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256
|

Is this OK (modulo the core2 setting)?

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] R optimization level?
parts:
On Fri, Nov 7, 2014 at 5:16 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
It's taking forever for models to compile for me in
the new RStan 2.5.  Seems like at least twice as long
as it used to, but I may be imagining things.

O3 is set in your ./R/Makevars.  Since you are talking about compile time, O3 might be relatively slow.  The way to compile file has not been changed in recent several releases in rstan, I don't see any reason in rstan 2.5 that causes what might be an imagination.

I want to make sure that in my RStan that I'm using
clang++ and -O3.  How do I do that?
Just following the script from the getting started  wiki should let you get there.

Also, see my post to stan-dev about setting mtune.  Right now,
it's set to core2, which isn't my architecture.
What post?

With Rob's help, I tracked down ~/.R/Makevars:

|
CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++
CXXFLAGS = -mtune=core2  -O3 $(LTO)     #set_by_rstan
R_XTRA_CPPFLAGS =  -I$(R_INCLUDE_DIR)      #set_by_rstanCC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256
CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256
CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256

CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256

CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256
|

Is this OK (modulo the core2 setting)?

This thing is copied from R's default CXXFLAGS.  I don't know what it does.  I guess you can set it to something else, but I think it is been there for quite long.  

$ grep CXXFLAGS /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/etc/Makeconf |grep LTO
CXXFLAGS = -Wall -mtune=core2 -g -O2 $(LTO) 




- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] R optimization level?
parts:
I believe -mtune=core2 sets optimization for all the Intel architectures beginning with the old "Core2", so it includes the newer multi-core instruction sets. In most cases, it'll be worth having it, I was told, but I admit I never ran a comparison.

Here's an Intel document that seems to indicate the same thing: 
https://software.intel.com/sites/products/documentation/doclib/iss/2013/compiler/cpp-lin/GUID-B915C718-BAAD-4816-9DC3-2B13DE9C9033.htm

Of course that means it can only be used on that machine, but most of the time I'm not compiling for someone else. I've never benchmarked Stan runs using different sets of machine instructions; it just takes the flags from my R compile.

Avi

use if you only need to compile for a single architecture.

The doc Richard sent indicates that there isn't a "native" setting
for the Intel compiler, but there is a "core2" setting. We definitely
want to turn the SSE instructions on.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] R optimization level?
parts:
By the way, I compiled two models under both rstan2.4 and rstan2.5.  It looks like that rstan2.5 does take a bit more time to compile, which I think it is due to the change in Stan. 

The R code I am running is 

$ more test.R
library("rstan", lib.loc = "./tmp")
system.time(stan_model("8schools.stan"))
system.time(stan_model("rats.stan"))

Under rstan2.4, "time Rscript test.R" gives

real 0m35.429s
user 0m34.296s
sys 0m1.059s

Under rstan2.5, it gives 

real 0m39.468s
user 0m38.181s
sys 0m1.214s


Jiqiang

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] R optimization level?
parts:
Actually, -march=native doesn't turn on every option (at least for GCC 4.6.2 which is the version at which Rtools for windows is currently frozen). For Sandy/Ivy bidge processors, my ad-hoc testing gives me the best average performance at:

-march=native -mtune=corei7-avx -msse2avx -mavx256-split-unaligned-load -mavx256-split-unaligned-store -mvzeroupper -O3 -std=gnu++0x --param l1-cache-line-size=64 --param l1-cache-size=32 --param l2-cache-size=256

Then again, I'm usually trying to compile R with OpenBLAS, so YMMV under a more vanilla install for Stan.

Avi
